thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-serving cluster us-east-1 — spike of CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS + container crashes on node gpu-23 (12 crashes in last 3m). paging errors showing up. paging oncall. <link-to-alert>
maria (oncall): I'm on it. tagging @kai and @sophia. any immediate customer impact known?
kai (runtime-eng): looking at recent logs. do we have any core dumps or nvml traces from gpu-23? please paste last 50 lines of pod stdout
maria (oncall): pasting quick tail from pod serving-abc-7f:
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:02Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS at deviceaddr 0x7fffb2a0
[2026-03-17T15:12:02Z] container exited with code 137
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] kernel: pagewalk: invalid PTE during async migration
```
kai (runtime-eng): hunch: device address wobble during pagewalk — looks like a kernel/PTE race with eviction under memory pressure. could be triggering illegal mem access in the runtime. not yet sure if runtime bug or kernel edge-case.
oncall-bot: Runbook step 1: cordon node -> `kubectl cordon gpu-23`. Step 2: drain -> `kubectl drain gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Step 3: start fallback model variant on alternate nodes. Autoplay: cordon started.
tim (eng-sre): cordon complete. ran drain command, 8/12 affected pods rescheduled. logs for remaining 4 show retry loops. executed: `kubectl drain gpu-23 --force --grace-period=30 --ignore-daemonsets`.
sophia (runtime-eng): do NOT hotpatch kernel on live node. runtime rollback might be faster. which revision pushed last night?
kai (runtime-eng): last deploy was v2026.03.16-build9. rolling back to v2026.03.02-build5 as a quick mitigation. starting rollout to dedicated pool only.
maria (oncall): customer-impact: ACME-Integrations and beta-app reported increased 5xx rate (~5-12% for 5m). CS looped in. preparing status update for high-touch customers.
customer-success-bot: Customer notification queued: short status update titled "Service degradation (GPU errors) — mitigations in progress". Sent to affected customers.
sophia (runtime-eng): mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback (quantized smaller model) on affected routes, 2) enforce temporary rate-limit at edge for heavy sequences, 3) increase prefix/KV cache to reduce kernel launches.
tim (eng-sre): fallback enabled, rate limit set to 75% for spike routes, autoscaler spun +3 gpu nodes in ded  pool. observed error rate drop to ~2%.
kai (runtime-eng): collecting nvml dumps and kernel trace (ftrace) from gpu-23 for vendor debugging. if we can repro with forced eviction we'll open bug with vendor/driver team. saving core dumps to /tmp/incident_6543219876/
maria (oncall): monitoring. if stable for 20m we'll start postmortem and customer follow-up. thanks all for rapid response. :white_check_mark:
